_comment: Curated nutrient->goal associations for FeedForward. base_weight in (0,1] is physiological association strength; evidence grade (A-D) is assigned in engine/evidence.py and modulates the final edge. Negative associations use type=negative: they are excluded from pathfinding, surfaced as warnings and penalise a food in proportion to how much of the daily limit one portion uses. type=enhancer marks a nutrient that helps the goal by improving absorption of another nutrient (vitamin C for non-heme iron): it is not a route on its own, it is applied through the bioavailability model and suggested as a meal pairing.

goal_edges.explanation: Protein provides the amino acids needed to repair and rebuild muscle tissue after exercise.
Protein supports general tissue repair and recovery.
Protein increases satiety, helping to regulate appetite.
Protein contributes to energy metabolism when other fuels are limited.
Carbohydrates are the body's primary and most readily available energy source.
Carbohydrates replenish glycogen stores critical for sustained endurance performance.
Dietary fat is an energy-dense fuel and supports absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.
Fibre adds bulk and supports regular, healthy digestion.
Fermentable fibre feeds beneficial gut bacteria.
Fibre slows glucose absorption, smoothing blood sugar response.
Soluble fibre helps lower LDL cholesterol.
Fibre promotes fullness and slows digestion, aiding weight control.
Iron is essential for haemoglobin and oxygen transport in the blood.
Iron is required to produce healthy red blood cells.
Iron supports oxygen delivery that drives cellular energy production.
Vitamin C supports normal immune cell function.
Vitamin C dramatically increases absorption of plant (non-heme) iron.
Vitamin C is a water-soluble antioxidant that neutralises free radicals.
Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis, supporting skin structure.
Calcium is the primary mineral in bone and maintains skeletal strength.
Calcium is required for normal muscle contraction and relaxation.
Vitamin D enables calcium absorption, essential for bone mineralisation.
Vitamin D modulates immune responses.
Vitamin D status is associated with mood regulation.
Magnesium supports the nervous system pathways involved in sleep.
Magnesium helps regulate the stress response and nervous system.
Magnesium supports muscle function and reduces cramping.
Magnesium is a structural component of bone.
Magnesium is a cofactor in hundreds of energy-producing reactions.
Zinc is essential for immune cell development and function.
Zinc supports skin repair and wound healing.
Zinc is involved in hair tissue growth and repair.
Zinc is required for thyroid hormone production.
Vitamin A is essential for the light-detecting pigments in the eye.
Vitamin A supports the integrity of immune barriers.
Vitamin A regulates skin cell turnover and repair.
Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant protecting cell membranes.
Vitamin E helps protect skin from oxidative damage.
Vitamin K activates proteins that bind calcium to bone.
Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting.
Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy triglyceride levels and heart function.
Omega-3 fatty acids have well-documented anti-inflammatory effects.
Omega-3 DHA is a major structural fat in the brain.
Omega-3 intake is associated with mood regulation.
Phosphorus works with calcium to build bone mineral.
Phosphorus is part of ATP, the cell's energy currency.
Manganese is a cofactor for antioxidant enzymes.
Manganese contributes to bone formation.
Excess sodium is associated with raised blood pressure and cardiovascular risk.
High sodium intake works against healthy blood pressure.
High saturated fat intake can raise LDL cholesterol.
Saturated fat works against healthy cholesterol levels.
Added sugars spike blood glucose and work against stable regulation.
Excess sugar contributes calories with low satiety.
Higher potassium intake is associated with lower blood pressure in dose-response meta-analyses of trials. This is an association, not a treatment.
Magnesium supplementation is associated with a modest reduction in blood pressure in randomised trials.
Calcium supplementation shows a small average blood-pressure effect in trial meta-analyses. The weight is kept low because the effect is modest and is not a reason to supplement.
Omega-3 intake is associated with lower joint inflammation in trial literature, including rheumatoid arthritis trials. This does not treat arthritis.
Vitamin C is required for collagen synthesis in connective tissue. The trial evidence is about collagen synthesis, not joint-disease outcomes.
Manganese is a cofactor in connective-tissue enzymes. The link to joint symptoms is mechanistic; no citation is attached, so this edge is low-confidence.
Magnesium supplementation improved insulin-sensitivity measures in meta-analyses of randomised trials. Not a diabetes treatment.
Higher fibre intake is associated with lower metabolic-syndrome risk in pooled observational evidence and reviews.
Omega-3 intake is associated with metabolic-syndrome markers in systematic reviews. The association is not a treatment claim.
Selenium is a cofactor for thyroid hormone metabolism. Trial evidence is concentrated in autoimmune thyroiditis and is not a recommendation to treat thyroid disease.
